A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text and Appendices A–E. The equations, table and all twelve figures can be matched despite relocation and reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer-training experiments, numerical sensitivity analyses and pretrained-LLM reasoning-trace measurements in Sections 4 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including multiplication accuracies in Table 1 and DeepSeek-R1/o1-mini reasoning-trace measurements, now displayed in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The UHAT model and CoT constructions for parity, NTT multiplication, median and BFS reachability are retained. The revised appendix proof does not alter these procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic parity, binary arithmetic, decimal median and DAG-reachability tasks, plus the same pretrained-LLM tasks. No evaluated dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same full, shortened, absent and dot-by-dot CoT comparisons where applicable, arithmetic decoding comparisons and NTT-versus-naive token-length comparison. New citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The splits, sample sizes, model configurations, training settings, metrics and LLM prompting/filtering procedures in Appendices C–D match. The added 'up to 16' qualification clarifies an existing experimental range.

E4.justification: CoT-length sweeps, dot-by-dot tests, digit-sensitivity analyses, numerical evidence for Conjecture C.5 and qualitative LLM-trace inspection are retained. Relocating the LLM plot adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages for parity, median and reachability, with three random seeds explicitly specified for median. Run information and plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains every result, including 99.96% for 14-digit and 99.83% for 16-digit multiplication. The plotted data and qualitative findings also match; v2 Figure 10 becomes v3 Figure 6 without new results.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2.2 revises the proof of Lemma C.6: the low-degree polynomial correlation argument is replaced by explicit Fourier-coefficient formulas, squared-coefficient bounds, Parseval's identity and a sensitivity calculation. The conditional lemma's statement and the principal theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The v3 introduction additionally claims that UHAT bounds entail bounds for fixed-precision softmax transformers, citing Jerad et al. (2025). The original lower-bound, tightness and algorithmic-task contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 makes the multiplication success qualification explicit as 'all lengths up to 16' and newly explains the resource constraint. The introduction adds a fixed-precision applicability argument, while the existing worst-case and alternative-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a code-repository link in a first-page footnote. v2 has no equivalent access information. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, data-generation instructions and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jerad et al. (2025) and a short mechanistic-CoT discussion citing Wang, Dutta and Kudo et al. (2024). Anonymous (2024) becomes Yang et al. (2025), matching the same paper title rather than adding another work.

P1.justification: There are localized wording and notation edits, an added Impact Statement, updated publication and acknowledgment text, and removal of the appendix contents list. The main section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The pretrained-LLM plot moves from Appendix D, Figure 10, to the main text as Figure 6, with an added appendix pointer. Other figures are renumbered or reflowed, and Figures 11–12 occupy separate pages. Graphic content and Table 1's structure are retained.

improvement.justification: The code pointer, explicit experimental scope and added research context provide limited benefits, while removal of the appendix contents reduces navigation. The rewritten Lemma C.6 defines coefficients using expectations with dependent product bits M(X,Y), then applies Parseval without justifying the required orthogonality; it therefore does not clearly repair v2's abbreviated argument. With the principal results unchanged, these mixed effects prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
